title: "Spring Cloud Ecosystem"
description: "A worked lesson in the shop-service microservices learning path."
---

**Source:** Supplied Spring Cloud course, Day 1 §1.3 and §2. **Example:** the shop system with Product, Order and User services.

## The problem: integration work multiplies

After separating Product, Order and User, the code is only part of the system. Order needs a Product address; calls need load balancing; a slow Product instance must not exhaust Order's resources; requests need tracing; operators need configuration control.

The supplied course introduces **Spring Cloud** as a family of Java/Spring integration projects for these recurring concerns. It also mentions other historical frameworks, including ServiceComb and ZeroC ICE. The architecture concepts matter more than one product's configuration.

## Group components by responsibility

| Responsibility | Course component | What it provides |
|---|---|---|
| Locate service instances | Eureka or Consul | Registry and service discovery |
| Choose an instance | Ribbon | Client-side load balancing |
| Express HTTP calls | Feign | Declarative client interface |
| Survive failing dependencies | Hystrix, Sentinel | Isolation, fallback, circuit breaking, limits |
| Provide one public entry point | Zuul, Spring Cloud Gateway | Routing and request filters |
| Follow requests across services | Sleuth, Zipkin | Tracing and trace collection |
| Publish events | Spring Cloud Stream | Broker-neutral messaging bindings |
| Manage distributed settings | Config, Bus, Apollo | Configuration distribution and refresh |

These components solve different problems. A gateway does not replace service discovery, and discovery does not make the network reliable.

## Equivalent ideas outside Java

We can illustrate an HTTP service with NestJS without reimplementing Spring Cloud. For example, a minimal Product endpoint might look like:

~~~ts
import { Controller, Get, Param } from '@nestjs/common';

@Controller('products')
export class ProductsController {
  @Get(':id')
  findOne(@Param('id') id: string) {
    return { id: Number(id), price: 100 };
  }
}
~~~

This is **an illustrative controller**, not a standalone NestJS project; the actual executable lab is dependency-free Node.js.

## Modernisation checkpoint

The course includes historical Spring Cloud integrations. For a new Spring application, inspect current Spring Cloud LoadBalancer, CircuitBreaker with Resilience4j, Spring Cloud Gateway, Micrometer Tracing and the **functional** Spring Cloud Stream model rather than assuming the old Ribbon, Hystrix, Zuul or Sleuth code still represents current practice.

## Select technology only after defining needs

For each component, state the failure or operational problem first. A system deployed to Kubernetes may already have DNS-based service discovery; adding a separate registry needs a justification.

## Review and extension

Explain this design to another engineer using the running example. Identify one benefit, one failure mode and the condition under which you would choose a simpler design.
